decisions.reason: As a broad, non-differentiated supplement line outside the firm's core pharmaceutical business, it is relatively likely to fall short of aspiration levels and be pruned despite available slack.
The skin-and-hair supplement has some market appeal but sits in a crowded pharmacy-adjacent segment, so a large pharma firm is likely to reallocate resources if performance is only middling.
Joint-health supplements fit established pharmacy demand reasonably well, so unless results are clearly below aspiration the firm can justify keeping it under organizational slack.
An immune-support supplement had a clearer differentiated positioning and likely benefited from heightened demand, making retention more likely than withdrawal.
Despite the valsartan-related problem signal in 2018, a generic blood-pressure drug is close to the firm's core capabilities, so management is more likely to correct and continue than to exit.
An over-the-counter migraine triptan fits the firm's established pharmaceutical and pharmacy-channel strengths, so it is likely to stay unless internal sales are clearly disappointing.
